prerequisites: Provide the SOC 2 report, security questionnaire, DPA, MSA, and vendor-risk framework.
Connect Drive, Microsoft 365, or Box as needed; Ironclad is optional for signed-contract verification.
entry.outcome: A cited risk memo with a go/no-go recommendation and accountable mitigation list.

steps.title: Assess the vendor
steps.prompt: Evaluate this vendor's security and contractual packet against our risk criteria and intended data access. Cite the document and section for every finding, reconcile contradictions between the questionnaire and independent evidence, and identify missing or stale materials. Recommend go, conditional go, or no-go under our framework, with required mitigations and proposed owners for human approval.

steps.title: Make the mitigation plan
steps.prompt: Prioritize unresolved findings by our risk tier and blocking criteria. For each, define the evidence or contract change needed, the responsible function, a target date, and the condition for closure. Keep unverified assurances separate from completed mitigations.

entry.title: Reproduce a paper's statistical results
entry.summary: Check published claims against the raw data and document the method behind each result.
prerequisites: Upload the manuscript, supplementary data, codebook, and any available analysis code.
Requires code execution and spreadsheet generation; missing methodological details may prevent exact reproduction.
entry.outcome: A reproducible statistical audit workbook with verified discrepancies and limitations.

steps.title: Audit the statistics
steps.prompt: Extract reported sample sizes, means, uncertainty measures, test statistics, and p-values from this paper. Reproduce each analysis from the supplied raw data using the stated methods where possible. Build a workbook comparing reported and recalculated values with formulas or code references. Check units, exclusions, paired observations, and multiplicity, and distinguish true discrepancies from rounding or insufficient information.

steps.title: Verify and explain the issues
steps.prompt: Check [figure] against the source data, including axes, error-bar definitions, and plotted values. Recheck every suspected discrepancy before drafting constructive reviewer comments that state the evidence, its implications, and the clarification or correction needed.

entry.title: Visualize program performance for stakeholders
entry.summary: Make participation, satisfaction, completion, and learning outcomes understandable across programs and periods.
prerequisites: Provide program data as CSV or XLSX, metric definitions, time periods, and audience priorities.
Requires code, spreadsheet, and presentation creation; Drive is optional for supporting context.
entry.outcome: A formula-driven dashboard and a concise visual board presentation.

steps.title: Build the visualization suite
steps.prompt: Inspect these program records for missing values, inconsistent definitions, and outliers before calculating results. Create an Excel dashboard comparing participation, completion, satisfaction, and pre/post learning measures by program and quarter. Then build an eight-to-ten-slide presentation emphasizing [audience priorities]. Use appropriate denominators, readable charts, and linked evidence; describe observed improvement without overstating causal impact.

steps.title: Add a meaningful comparison
steps.prompt: Break down [metrics] by [relevant demographic or location] where sample sizes support it. Research comparable benchmarks only if needed, document differences in definitions and populations, and add reference lines only when the comparison is defensible.

entry.title: Explore a difficult concept with an interactive model
entry.summary: Use linked visuals and controls to see the mechanism behind an explanation.
prerequisites: Describe what you understand and the precise part that remains unclear.
Requires an interactive visualization environment.
entry.outcome: A manipulable explanation and a short diagnostic quiz.

steps.title: Show the mechanism
steps.prompt: I understand [known behavior] but cannot explain [specific mechanism]. Build an interactive visualization around that gap, with controls for the important variables and linked views showing what changes and what stays conserved. For an orbital-motion example, connect position, speed, and energy rather than simply animating a planet. State the simplifying assumptions.

steps.title: Test my understanding
steps.prompt: Change [one parameter or condition] while preserving the same visual structure, then ask me to predict what happens before revealing it. Explain errors in my reasoning and finish with a short account I could reproduce without the animation.

entry.title: Triage escalations and alert people only for critical cases
entry.summary: Apply your severity rules, connect related tickets, and route work without paging everyone.
prerequisites: Requires a proactive channel assistant with write access to Zendesk, Intercom, or Jira Service Management.
Provide severity definitions, ownership rules, and the P1 contact; PagerDuty is optional for incident checks.
entry.outcome: An organized escalation queue with first-response drafts and targeted critical alerts.

steps.title: Set the triage responsibility
steps.prompt: For each new escalation in [channel], apply our severity definitions, compare it with existing tickets, and link or merge verified duplicates according to our support rules. Tag the owning team and draft a first customer response for an agent to review. Alert a person only when the case meets P1 criteria, stating the evidence and decision needed.

steps.title: Review the queue
steps.prompt: Summarize escalations since [time], highlighting [priority category], unresolved owners, and cases requiring a human decision. Apply this correction to [ticket]: [severity or owner correction], and update the channel's rules only where I explicitly request a lasting change.

entry.title: Prepare context and agendas for next week's calls
entry.summary: Gather previous discussion and open commitments into one readable meeting-prep document.
prerequisites: Connect Google Calendar, Slack, and Gmail; Drive is optional for documents.
Provide agenda preferences, exclusions, and the planning folder; recurring delivery requires a scheduler.
entry.outcome: A week-ahead briefing with a short agenda for every meeting and three prep priorities.

steps.title: Prepare the meeting week
steps.prompt: Review my calendar for [week]. For each meeting, find the last relevant discussion, related messages, referenced documents, and commitments I owe. Draft one compact agenda paragraph and link the source context. Flag the three meetings that need the most preparation and explain why, then save one combined week-ahead document.

steps.title: Create a weekly routine
steps.prompt: Schedule this briefing for [weekday, time, timezone], covering the following week. Save the combined brief and individual agendas in a dated folder under [Planning], carry forward unresolved prep items, and state which sources were unavailable on each run.

entry.title: Post a weekly team status from actual work
entry.summary: Combine team conversation and tracker state into a digest people can correct before forwarding.
prerequisites: Requires a channel assistant with scheduled routines and access to Linear or Jira.
GitHub is optional for merged pull requests; define channels, tracker scope, schedule, and timezone.
entry.outcome: A recurring channel update with decisions, open work, and blocked owners.

steps.title: Schedule the team digest
steps.prompt: Every [weekday, time, timezone], post a draft weekly update in [team channel] using this channel's discussions and the connected tracker. Cover decisions made, work completed, items still open, and dependencies waiting on named owners. Link evidence, check current ticket state, and distinguish shipped work from tickets merely marked complete.

steps.title: Expand and correct the digest
steps.prompt: Include [additional channel], [repository], and [launch tracker] in the next run. Show how long each blocked item has been stuck against plan and its owner. Apply these corrections: [details], then list the configured schedule and sources so the team can verify the routine.

entry.title: Compare grants by opportunity and effort
entry.summary: See award size, uncertainty, deadline, and preparation load together before choosing what to pursue.
prerequisites: Provide your grant pipeline with awards, deadlines, effort estimates, and success-rate evidence where available.
Requires interactive visualization and current official-program research for deadlines and eligibility.
entry.outcome: An explorable grant comparison and a realistic submission schedule.

steps.title: Map the grant choices
steps.prompt: Compare these grant opportunities across award amount, estimated chance, deadline, eligibility, and effort. Build a linked chart and table with filters, flag near-term deadlines, and verify current requirements on official pages. Label uncertain success estimates and omit expected-value calculations where the inputs are unsupported. Help me shortlist options under [capacity constraint].

steps.title: Work back from deadlines
steps.prompt: For the shortlisted grants due within [90 days], build a submission timeline working backward from verified deadlines, including partner input and internal review. Mark [submitted grant] as in progress and reprioritize the remaining workload without losing its follow-up obligations.

entry.title: Design a practical workflow improvement
entry.summary: Capture the actual process before choosing tools or introducing automation.
prerequisites: Provide current process documents, sample inputs and outputs, and concrete pain points.
Interactive form support is optional; tool connections depend on the solution selected.
entry.outcome: A completed process assessment and implementation materials suited to real constraints.

steps.title: Build the process assessment
steps.prompt: Create a fillable assessment for [workflow]. Capture the trigger, frequency, volume, steps, people, inputs, outputs, decisions, bottlenecks, error patterns, tools, constraints, and success measures. Include prompts for specific examples and an exportable summary I can return for solution design. Make missing facts visible rather than filling them with generic assumptions.

steps.title: Design within our constraints
steps.prompt: Use my completed assessment and samples to propose a practical improvement. Explain which steps benefit from AI, which need human judgment, and which require connectors or ordinary automation. Provide example prompts, templates, setup steps, and a small measurable pilot that fits [budget, skills, and access constraints].

entry.title: Write an impact report grounded in program evidence
entry.summary: Connect verified outcomes and financial stewardship with an authentic story for your stakeholders.
prerequisites: Provide participant, attendance, outcome, volunteer, finance, and qualitative-feedback records.
Requires data analysis, document creation, and chart generation; use only authorized participant stories.
entry.outcome: A designed impact report with cited metrics, clear charts, and audience-specific versions.

steps.title: Build the report
steps.prompt: Analyze these records for [organization and reporting period]. First reconcile the key metrics, then create a report with an executive overview, program context, reach and demographics, outcomes, finances, and next-year goals. Use clear visualizations and only supplied, authorized stories or quotations. Separate measured outcomes from causal claims and flag incomplete data instead of inventing an impact narrative.

steps.title: Tailor the evidence
steps.prompt: Create three concise versions: one for funders emphasizing outcomes and cost-effectiveness, one for donors using verified human stories, and one for the board covering strategic implications and operational risks. Keep every number consistent with the approved report and show the source of each headline claim.
